office_does: A Pierce County District Court judge hears misdemeanor and gross misdemeanor cases, traffic infractions, protection orders and civil claims up to $100,000 for a four-year term; the discretion is mostly in pretrial release, sentencing and therapeutic-court supervision.
race_blurb: Judge Jeanette Lineberry is retiring from Position 8 and endorses Sven Nelson, a 30-year Pierce County deputy prosecutor and judge pro tem. His opponent, James Armstrong, is a civil-practice attorney and Marine veteran who was presiding judge of Bremerton Municipal Court in 2025. Only two filed, so there was no primary.

candidates.summary: Pierce County deputy prosecuting attorney since 1996, former team chief of the Special Assault, Elder Abuse and Property Crimes units, and a judge pro tempore since 2019.
highlights: Deputy prosecutor since 1996; team chief of the Special Assault, Elder Abuse and Property Crimes units [S1][S3]
Judge pro tempore since 2019, presiding over jury trials, sentencings and community court [S1][S3]
Says 'accountability and rehabilitation are not opposites' and that restorative justice 'should never minimize accountability' [S3]
Rated Exceptionally Well Qualified by the Tacoma-Pierce County Bar Association [S5]
Endorsed by retiring Position 8 Judge Lineberry; campaign lists most Pierce County judges, police and firefighter unions, and both county parties [S1][S2]

experience.basis: Runs on about 30 years in the county prosecutor's office and seven years pro tem, with the retiring incumbent's endorsement; an institutional record, though no full-time bench service.

safety.basis: Formation is three decades of prosecution focused on victims of sexual assault and elder abuse; open to treatment and community-court options but frames them within accountability and cautions against restorative approaches that minimize it.

candidates.summary: Kent/Auburn workers' compensation and disability attorney, Marine Corps veteran and judge pro tem who served as presiding judge of Bremerton Municipal Court in 2025.
highlights: Presiding judge of Bremerton Municipal Court in 2025; about four years as a judge pro tem [S2][S4]
Civil practice in workers' compensation, Social Security disability and personal injury since 2000 [S4][S5]
Emphasizes treatment-based rehabilitation (substance use, mental health, DV-MRT), restorative justice and concern about legal financial obligations [S2]
Rated Exceptionally Well Qualified by JAJEC; not on TPCBA's 2026 ratings list [S6][S7]
No campaign website found; statement lists no endorsements [S1]

experience.basis: Runs on 26 years of practice, a year as a full-time presiding municipal judge (confirmed by the WSBA's judicial-service record) and pro tem service; a record-based pitch rather than an outsider case.

safety.basis: Civil rather than prosecutorial formation; makes treatment-based rehabilitation and restorative justice his stated priority and criticizes legal financial obligations, while keeping accountability in the frame.
